nodes.label: Signature block
nodes.rationale: Settled as the single word for the whole printed block (label, name, printed title) after 'signing line' had been used loosely for both the block and its label.

nodes.label: Caption
nodes.rationale: A title printed on the paper itself ('Driver', 'Section Incharge', 'GSU Representative'). The test is where the words come from, not what they look like: a caption is identical under any name, so the system stores nothing for it. This realisation removed roughly half the storage problem and killed the separate signatory table.

nodes.label: employee_history table
nodes.rationale: Holds one dated version of a person's name, position title and short form so an old document keeps the wording it was printed with. Built 31 August 2026; the current columns stay on employee as a copy written in the same transaction, because reading a name is the common case and reaching through history rows everywhere would be a lot of code for no gain.

nodes.label: employee_history_correction log
nodes.rationale: A spelling fix edits a version in place and corrects every document at once, which would otherwise leave no trace; the log records field, old value, new value and who did it so the repair stays accountable.

nodes.label: Position title short form
nodes.rationale: Documents print 'AO-I/Supply Officer', not 'Administrative Officer I (Supply Officer)'; the boxes on the paper are small. No rule worth trusting derives one from the other, so somebody types it once. One person has exactly one short form, so it lives on the employee rather than per document.

nodes.label: Documents store a reference, never typed text
nodes.rationale: Storing the name as text freezes both a real name change and a typo the same way. If 30 records were saved with a misspelled name nobody would remember which 30. A link to a history row lets a correction reach every record and a marriage leave old records alone.

nodes.label: Config table
nodes.rationale: One row per setting, key fixed in code and plain-text value filled in by the office, so no row id is hardcoded. Typed columns were rejected because only one row would ever use them; a short fixed code column on org_unit was rejected because an admin-populated but non-editable field confuses whoever maintains office data. Lives at src/lib/server/db/schema/config.ts with CONFIG_KEYS beside it so a typo is a type error.

nodes.label: org.gsu_unit setting
nodes.rationale: Names the org unit whose staff may be offered on a GSU-restricted block. Renamed from fuel.gsu_org_unit on 7 September 2026 because which unit is the General Services Unit is a fact about the office, not about fuel, and two documents read it — a per-report copy could disagree with itself.

nodes.label: fuel.usual_approver setting
nodes.rationale: An optional default employee id, added 8 September 2026 after fuel.penr_officer was removed. It only decides which name the form starts with; nothing is restricted and nothing is fixed. A stored id belonging to somebody separated simply reads as empty rather than warning anyone.

nodes.label: Signatories page (/admin/signatories)
nodes.rationale: A tab per report, and inside a tab one row per setting rather than one row per document: four rows would be four controls over two stored values, promising an independence that does not exist. Placed next to Organizational Structure but kept separate because this is signatory configuration, not office structure.

nodes.label: Org unit guard (src/lib/server/org-unit-guard.ts)
nodes.rationale: One function answering whether an org unit is named by a setting, called by both the delete and deactivate paths in src/routes/admin/org-structure/+page.server.ts. A real foreign key would only have protected deletion; deactivation is an ordinary column change no foreign key can catch, so one mechanism covering both beats two covering one each. The cost, accepted knowingly, is that it holds only while every path goes through it.

nodes.label: The selection list is built from the document's filed date
nodes.rationale: The form asks who was valid on the filed date, comparing valid_from and valid_until, rather than who is working today. Reopening last month's slip still offers last month's people, a slip filed today does not, and editing needs no special case. Separation must therefore close the current history row, not only change the status.

nodes.label: Somebody no longer working is never offered and never saves
nodes.rationale: Any employment_status other than active counts as not working. No warning is raised when somebody is marked separated: the next person to prepare a slip finds them gone and picks whoever signs now, which is how the office already works.

nodes.label: Signature blocks are fixed in the code
nodes.rationale: Blocks sit in fixed positions on the printed page. An admin-editable list would let the layout be broken, so the set of blocks is program and database structure, one column per block holding an employee history reference or nothing. The known cost is that adding or renaming a block is developer work.

nodes.label: Signing happens on paper only
nodes.rationale: The system prepares and prints the correct names; the paper is carried around and signed by hand. An earlier answer saying signing happened both on paper and in the system created a problem that no longer exists — signers without an account could never approve, so 'not signed yet' and 'never signed here' were indistinguishable.

nodes.label: Per procurationem (p.p.) signing
nodes.rationale: Signing on somebody else's behalf with their authority, confirmed on four blocks of the real CDS copies. Entirely invisible to the system: the printed name never changes and everything the substitute adds is handwritten.

nodes.label: OIC (Officer-in-Charge)
nodes.rationale: Two senses at this office: the standing OIC who has held the post for years and whose name is printed, and temporary cover for a few days that is only ever handwritten. Neither needs anything built.

nodes.label: Requisition and Issue Slip (RIS)
nodes.rationale: The only fuel document printing real position titles, which is why it drives the employee history requirement; its 'Approved by' was wrongly recorded as a fixed string 'OIC, PENR Officer' and is in fact a picked person whose own title prints.

nodes.label: Fuel report
nodes.rationale: Not one form but three documents printed together, which corrected Topic 5's assumption that a report equals a form; the decision survived and now applies per document.

nodes.label: Supplier signature block
nodes.rationale: The gasoline station owner or their staff is not an employee and not in the system. Handled by the block's rule being 'nobody may be chosen' and printing blank, rather than by inventing a record for them.

nodes.label: Employee and user separation
nodes.rationale: Option 1, full separation, was chosen over leaving employees only for non-users (people would live in two tables) and over letting user be the employee table (login code would have to exclude password-less rows forever, easy to get wrong). Built; details in .claude/docs/features/employee-and-user-separation.md.

nodes.label: Group designation title
nodes.rationale: A title on a Technical Working Group, association or BAC Secretariat is printed on the paper, so it is a caption and needs no mechanism. Group titles appear on that group's own memoranda rather than on the fill-in forms this project handles, and are never reused across documents. This settlement also retired the coined terms 'position signatory' and 'designation signatory'.

nodes.label: One person may fill two blocks of the same document
nodes.rationale: Allowed with no warning. The user watched an office head approve their own leave application when the admin officer was away; that observed case outweighed the written rule. It is the document, not the person, that decides whether one name may fill two blocks.

nodes.label: Add name or position change dialog
nodes.rationale: src/routes/admin/employees/add-change-dialog.svelte. Ends the current history row and starts a new one — the 'record a change that happened' path.

nodes.label: Correct this entry dialog
nodes.rationale: src/routes/admin/employees/correct-entry-dialog.svelte, opened from name-position-history-sheet.svelte. Edits a row in place — the 'fix a mistake in what was typed' path — and carries the warning headed 'This corrects what is already filed'. Two separate entry points replaced the originally planned single Save button that asked which kind of change it was.

nodes.label: The separate signatory table was removed
nodes.rationale: The whole design had rested on the assumption that a signatory is a person with a typed name and typed position title in a table of their own. Real fuel documents examined 27 August 2026 showed nobody's title is ever typed: it is a caption, or fixed, or read from the person's record. Cost an edit and nothing more, because nothing had been built. A per-report signatory table was also rejected: anybody signing two kinds of document would need a row in each, so a spelling fix would have to be repeated.

nodes.label: Rule: who may be chosen for a block
nodes.rationale: Any employee, only staff of a named unit, or nobody at all. Only a restricted list needs a rule and only the GSU one is restricted. Choosing the wrong eligible person is not the system's problem — GSU simply refuses to sign; the system only stops what is impossible.

nodes.label: Rule: where the printed title comes from
nodes.rationale: Two answers only: nothing is printed because the form carries a caption, or the person's own position title as it stood at the time. There is no third rule for a fixed string written into the program.

nodes.label: Where a default name comes from
nodes.rationale: Partly settled. Three sources: set by an admin (the fuel approver), worked out by the report (RIS 'Requested by' defaults to whoever is entering), or set by whoever handles the report (raised, not yet needed). The rule is not 'defaults are never configured' but 'configured here only when nothing else can work it out'.

nodes.label: General Services Unit (GSU)
nodes.rationale: There is only one General Services Unit and any of its staff may approve any section's slip; an earlier sketch giving the roster its own org unit so GSU and CDS copies expected different people was wrong and was dropped.
